supporting_observations.claim: The periodic outbound activity is attributable to ledgerlinkupd.exe running from max.fischer's user-profile AppData directory, rather than the inventoried C:\Program Files\LedgerLink updater location.

The updater made repeated proxy CONNECT requests to update.ledgerlink.co:443, with successful tunnels around five-minute intervals from 13:44 through 14:09; the first observed request at 13:39 received a gateway error.

The observed destination is update.ledgerlink.co, while the inventory identifies update.ledgerlink.com as the approved LedgerLink update service. This domain mismatch and the user-profile executable path are suspicious, but do not alone establish malicious activity.

The periodic timing and executable name are consistent with the inventory's description of LedgerLink checking for updates about every five minutes, which provides a plausible benign explanation for the alerted pattern.

known_telemetry_limitations: Proxy records show CONNECT destinations and tunnel byte counts, but the available records do not establish the TLS certificate, server identity, or contents of the tunneled exchanges.
The supplied collection outage affects WS-LWARD-01, not the alerted WS-MFISCHER-01; it does not explain or resolve the uncertainty in the alerted activity.
claims_not_established: Whether update.ledgerlink.co is a legitimate LedgerLink domain, an approved alias, or an unauthorized lookalike.
Whether the AppData executable is an authentic LedgerLink updater or a renamed/replaced binary.
Whether the successful tunnels carried legitimate update-check traffic or malicious content.
additional_evidence_needed: Obtain the updater's hash, signature, file metadata, and installation or download provenance; compare them with a known-good LedgerLink release.
Validate update.ledgerlink.co with LedgerLink or an authoritative vendor source, and collect DNS, TLS certificate, and destination reputation/ownership evidence.
Collect endpoint or proxy content-level evidence sufficient to identify what the successful tunnels exchanged.
unrelated_findings: Cisco AnyConnect vpnagent.exe started on WS-MFISCHER-01; the inventory says the organization has no VPN. Investigate separately; this process is not shown making the alerted connections. (T245-00148, T245-00149)

A UserAssist registry value records activity associated with mstsc.exe, which may merit separate review given the stated remote-administration practice. It is not evidence about the alerted HTTPS connections. (T245-00162)
